title: Seville Slow: Mudéjar Courtyards and Triana Nights

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (42°C is routine and the city genuinely shuts 14:00–20:00); Semana Santa and Feria de Abril triple hotel rates and close monuments.

accommodation.note: Casa-palacio guesthouse double, per-person share, Santa Cruz or Alfalfa

food.note: Tapas €3.50–5 each, menú del día €14–18, one €45 dinner

transport.note: Tussam card, AVE/Media Distancia day trip, airport bus both ways

activities.note: Alcázar, Cathedral, Casa de Pilatos, Setas, flamenco, Córdoba Mezquita

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — flat city, 7–10 km a day, but heat is the limiting factor, not gradient.

gatewayAirport: SVQ — Seville Airport; EA airport bus to Plaza de Armas 35 min (€4 single), taxi flat fare ~€25–33
summary: Seville is a city of interiors: the whole point is what happens behind the door, in the courtyard, under the vine. This week is built around that — the Real Alcázar's Mudéjar rooms at opening hour, Casa de Pilatos's Renaissance-Roman patio in the empty midday, the Hospital de los Venerables's sunken courtyard fountain, and Triana's tiled bar fronts across the river at night. Days follow the Andalusian clock: monuments before 12:00, a long lunch, siesta, then the city reopens at 20:00 and stays up. Distances are small and flat; the discipline is timing, not stamina. A Córdoba or Cádiz day by fast train supplies the contrast.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Alfalfa and the first tapas crawl
itinerary.morning: EA bus in from SVQ, drop bags, orient on **Plaza de la Alfalfa**. Coffee and *tostada con manteca colorá* at **Bar El Comercio**, Calle Lineros 9, a 1904 tiled churro bar.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Setas de Sevilla** (Metropol Parasol) walkway (€16 including the Antiquarium's Roman house mosaics beneath) and Plaza de la Encarnación. Then the **Iglesia del Salvador** (€5, or included on the Cathedral combined ticket), a Baroque hall on a mosque footprint.
itinerary.evening: Crawl three bars: **Bodeguita Romero** (Calle Harinas 10, *pringá* roll), **Bar Las Teresas** (Calle Santa Teresa 2, jamón), **Casa Morales** (Calle García de Vinuesa 11, vermouth from the vats).
itinerary.dayStats: 5.8 km walked, flat; EA bus €4; Setas 09:30–00:30; tapas €3.50–5 each, three bars ~€30pp.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Casa 1800, Calle Rodrigo Caro 6, Santa Cruz.

itinerary.title: Real Alcázar at opening, then Santa Cruz
itinerary.morning: **Real Alcázar** on the 09:30 opening slot (€15.50, +€5.50 for the Cuarto Real Alto; 09:30–19:00 April–September, to 17:00 in winter). Head straight to the Patio de las Doncellas before the groups, then the Salón de Embajadores dome and out into the Jardines with the Galería de Grutesco.
itinerary.afternoon: **Hospital de los Venerables** (Plaza de los Venerables 8, €12) for the sunken patio and Velázquez's *Santa Rufina*, then wander Callejón del Agua and Plaza de Doña Elvira in the emptier siesta hours.
itinerary.evening: Flamenco at **Casa de la Memoria**, Calle Cuna 6 — 90 minutes, no amplification, ~€22, book ahead. Late dinner at **Casa Ricardo**, Calle Hernán Cortés 2.

itinerary.title: Cathedral, Giralda and the riverside
itinerary.morning: **Catedral de Sevilla + Giralda** on a 10:00 slot (€14, €13 online) — the Almohad minaret's ramps were built for a horseman, not stairs; the Capilla Mayor retablo is the largest altarpiece in Christendom. Then the free **Archivo General de Indias** across the square.
itinerary.afternoon: **Torre del Oro** (€3) and the Guadalquivir bank, then **Plaza de España** and the Parque de María Luisa in late light — go at 18:30 when the ceramic province benches face west.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Cañabota**, Calle Orfila 3 — Atlantic fish over coals, counter seating, book 2–3 weeks, €55–75pp. Alternative: **Casa Robles** for the classic version.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.1 km; Cathedral 10:45–18:00 Mon–Sat, Sun from 14:30; Archivo free, closed Mondays.

itinerary.title: Córdoba day trip by AVE
itinerary.morning: Santa Justa 08:00–08:30 AVE/Avant to Córdoba, 45–50 min. Walk 20 min to the **Mezquita-Catedral** for the 08:30–09:30 free early entry (Mon–Sat, no ticket, no groups) or the 10:00 paid slot (€13). The 856 double-arched columns of Abd al-Rahman's hall are the reason to make the trip.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Judería** lanes, **Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos** (€5), and Calleja de las Flores. Lunch of *salmorejo* and *flamenquín* at **Bodegas Campos**, Calle de Lineros 32.
itinerary.evening: Back on the 19:00–20:00 train. Late tapas at **Eslava**, Calle Eslava 3 in San Lorenzo (the *costilla* and the cigar-shaped *huevo sobre bizcocho*), no reservations for the bar.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.9 km walked in Córdoba; AVE 45–50 min, €25–38 return; Mezquita free 08:30–09:30 Mon–Sat.

itinerary.title: Casa de Pilatos, Macarena and the convents
itinerary.morning: **Casa de Pilatos** (Plaza de Pilatos 1, €12 full house, €10 ground floor only; free for EU citizens Mondays 15:00–18:00). The main patio's Roman busts, Genoese marble and Mudéjar *azulejo* dado in one square is the city's argument in miniature.
itinerary.afternoon: North up Calle San Luis through **Macarena**: the Baroque **Iglesia de San Luis de los Franceses** (€6), the **Basílica de la Macarena** and her Virgin (€5 museum), and the surviving Almohad **Muralla** stretch. Buy convent sweets through the *torno* at **Convento de Santa Paula**.
itinerary.evening: **Alameda de Hércules** — vermouth at **Bar Bulebar**, then dinner at **Sobretablas**, Calle Colombia 7 (book 1–2 weeks, €45–60pp) or the closer **Casa Ruperto** for quail.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.6 km; Pilatos €12, 09:00–18:00; San Luis closed Mondays; convent sweets €6–9 a box, cash.

itinerary.title: Triana across the river
itinerary.morning: Cross the **Puente de Isabel II** (1852, Gustavo Steinacher and Ferdinand Bernadet, modelled on the Pont du Carrousel) to the **Centro Cerámica Triana** (€2.10) built over the old Santa Ana kiln floors — the tile industry that surfaced half the city's façades.
itinerary.afternoon: **Mercado de Triana** for lunch at the counters, then Calle Betis for the classic river-facing view of the Torre del Oro, and the **Capilla de los Marineros**. Browse the surviving tile workshops on Calle Antillano Campos.
itinerary.evening: Triana flamenco with less theatre: **Casa Anselma**, Calle Pagés del Corro 49, opens around midnight, no sign, no entry fee, drinks-only, and no photographs. Eat first at **Blanca Paloma**, Calle San Jacinto 49.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.2 km; Centro Cerámica €2.10, 11:00–18:00; Anselma from ~00:00, closed Sundays.

itinerary.title: Fine art and departure
itinerary.morning: **Museo de Bellas Artes** in the Convento de la Merced (free for EU citizens, €1.50 otherwise) — the Zurbarán and Murillo rooms in the former church nave are the best-hung pictures in Andalucía.
itinerary.afternoon: Last vermouth and a *serranito* at **Bodega Santa Cruz "Las Columnas"**, Calle Rodrigo Caro 1, then bags and the EA bus to SVQ from Prado de San Sebastián.
itinerary.dayStats: 3.9 km; Bellas Artes 09:00–21:00 Tue–Sat, closed Mondays; EA bus 35 min, €4; allow 2 h at SVQ.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Casa 1800
accommodationStrategy.description: Thirty-odd rooms in a 19th-century house one lane from the Alcázar wall, with a roof terrace looking straight at the Giralda and free afternoon tea. You can be first through the Alcázar gate five minutes after breakfast. €180–260 double; ask for an interior patio room to escape the Mateos Gago noise.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Palacio de Villapanés
accommodationStrategy.description: An 18th-century palace with a proper Baroque staircase, a courtyard pool and enough distance from Santa Cruz to feel residential while staying a 10-minute walk from the Cathedral. €200–290.

accommodationStrategy.name: Corral del Rey
accommodationStrategy.description: Thirteen rooms in a 17th-century *casa señorial* with Roman columns in the courtyard, dropped into the best tapas grid in the city. €190–280; the roof plunge pool is the July argument.

logistics.connectivity: Full EU roaming; 5G throughout the centre and on the AVE corridor. Renfe requires the app or a printed ticket for barrier entry at Santa Justa.
logistics.emergency: 112. Municipal police 092. Pharmacies rotate a *farmacia de guardia* — the roster is posted on every pharmacy door. EU/EHIC applies; Spain's public system is straightforward for EU visitors.
logistics.weather: The *terral*, a dry inland wind, pushes July–August highs past 42°C; Seville regularly records Spain's national maximum. Even in May, 15:00–18:00 is for interiors. November brings short, heavy Atlantic rain.
logistics.bookingWindows: Real Alcázar 1–2 weeks (official infoticketing site only — resellers add 40%); Cathedral 3–5 days; Casa de la Memoria 4–7 days; Cañabota and Sobretablas 1–3 weeks; AVE to Córdoba 2–3 weeks for the cheap fare buckets.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards work almost everywhere, but old-guard bars (Casa Morales, Casa Anselma, convent *tornos*) are cash. Tipping is minimal — round up, or leave €1–2 per person after tapas.
logistics.transportRules: Validate the Tussam card on boarding; the EA bus takes cards. Renfe security-scans bags at Santa Justa — arrive 20 minutes before an AVE departure.
logistics.permits: Andalucía charges no municipal tourist tax as of 2026. The Alcázar and Cathedral both refuse large backpacks — no cloakroom at the Alcázar. Flamenco venues like Casa Anselma prohibit photography outright and will ask you to leave.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable. Heat is the hazard: carry 2 litres, walk the *sombra* side, treat 14:00–17:00 in summer as unwalkable. Petty theft concentrates on Calle Sierpes and the Cathedral perimeter.

proTips: The Alcázar's free slot is **Mondays 18:00–18:30, October–March**, released online only and gone within hours — set a reminder for the release, and note it is far too short for the gardens.
Córdoba's **Mezquita is free 08:30–09:30, Monday to Saturday**, with no ticket required and no tour groups. Take the 08:00 AVE and you are inside the arcades in near-silence.
Casa de Pilatos is **free to EU citizens on non-holiday Mondays, 15:00–18:00** — exactly the hours when everything else is shut for siesta.
Order tapas *de pie* at the bar, not at a table: the same plate costs 20–30% more seated on a terrace, and every price list posts both tariffs.
Book the **Giralda climb for the last hour before closing** — the ramp empties, and the bells at the hour from inside the belfry are worth the timing.
**Casa Anselma** has no sign and no fee; look for the plain door at Pagés del Corro 49 after midnight and buy a drink. It is the antidote to ticketed *tablao* flamenco.
Buy convent sweets through the revolving *torno* at Santa Paula — you never see the nun, you leave exact change, and the *dulce de membrillo* travels.
In heat, use the **Setas walkway at 09:30 or after 21:00**; the deck is unshaded and the midday version is punishing for the same €16.

raw.Walkable blocks: Santa Cruz (Calle Mateos Gago → Plaza de Doña Elvira → Callejón del Agua, 1.1 km of shaded lanes); Alfalfa/Encarnación (Plaza de la Alfalfa → Calle Pérez Galdós → Setas, 900 m); Alameda de Hércules (the 800 m boulevard itself, plus Calle Feria); Macarena (Basílica → Calle San Luis → Convento de Santa Paula, 1.3 km); Triana (Puente de Isabel II → Calle Betis → Calle San Jacinto → Mercado de Triana, 1.6 km).
raw.Transit pass: Tussam's **Tarjeta Multiviaje** — €1.50 refundable deposit, top-ups from €7, fares around €0.76 per ride versus €1.40 cash on board; the single Metro Line 1 and the T1 tram to San Bernardo take the same card. Most of this week needs zero transit.
raw.Airport transfer: **EA (Especial Aeropuerto)** bus, airport → Prado de San Sebastián → Plaza de Armas, every 20–30 min, ~35 min, €4 single / €6 return. Taxis run a fixed municipal tariff, roughly €25 weekday daytime, €33 nights and holidays.
raw.Booking timeline: **Real Alcázar** — timed entry, book 1–2 weeks ahead on alcazardesevilla.infoticketing.com (the only official channel); the free Monday evening slot (18:00–18:30, October–March) releases online and vanishes within hours. **Cathedral + Giralda** — 3–5 days ahead, €14 at the door or €13 online. **Flamenco at Casa de la Memoria** — 4–7 days, only 100 seats. **Córdoba AVE** — book 2–3 weeks for the €25–35 fare band.
raw.Architectural focal points: Almohad brickwork in the Giralda's sebka panelling (1184–98, Ahmad ibn Baso); Pedro I's 1360s Mudéjar palace inside the Alcázar, built by Toledan and Granadan craftsmen for a Christian king; Casa de Pilatos's 1520s fusion of Gothic, Mudéjar and Italian Renaissance; Leonardo de Figueroa's Baroque at the Hospital de los Venerables (1687); Aníbal González's 1929 regionalist Plaza de España; Jürgen Mayer's 2011 timber Metropol Parasol.
raw.Eating structure: stand-up tapas bars in Alfalfa and Santa Cruz, sit-down *guisos* in Triana, market lunch at Feria or Triana. Only the destination kitchens (Cañabota, Sobretablas) require booking; classic bars are elbows-only.
raw.Day trip: **Córdoba** by Renfe AVE/Avant, Santa Justa → Córdoba in 45–50 min, €25–38 return depending how early you book; Media Distancia takes 1h20 for less.

sources.verified: Real Alcázar admission (€15.50), Cuarto Real Alto supplement (€5.50) and seasonal hours (09:30–19:00 Apr–Sep, to 17:00 Oct–Mar) confirmed on alcazarsevilla.org, which names alcazardesevilla.infoticketing.com as the sole official channel. sources.confidenceNotes: Tussam Multiviaje fare and deposit, the €4 EA bus fare and the fixed taxi tariff all drift annually. AVE Seville–Córdoba pricing is dynamic; €25–38 assumes 2–3 weeks' notice. The Mezquita free hour and the Alcázar/Casa de Pilatos free slots are the most volatile items and are periodically suspended. Restaurant lead times and Casa Anselma's opening nights need re-confirmation.
